svg.text: v9 — Vector search inside PostgreSQL (pgvector + HNSW index)
PROBLEM: v8 copied EVERY vector of the organisation into Python for each question — 10.5 s P50 at 50,000 chunks (the maths was 36 ms).
FIX: store vectors in a pgvector column; PostgreSQL compares them itself and walks an HNSW index; only the best 5 rows leave the database.
API PROCESS — GET /documents/search?mode=semantic
router.py → service.py (unchanged since v8)
q="Can I get my money back?" → embeddings.py → [0.02, −0.11, … 384 numbers]
repository.py — semantic_search (rewritten)
SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order
SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = 100
SELECT … , embedding <=> :question AS distance
WHERE organization_id = :org AND embedding_model = :m
ORDER BY distance LIMIT 5
384 numbers in, 5 rows out
PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector 0.8.6 (docker/postgres/Dockerfile, new)
document_chunks.embedding vector(384) (was bytea in v8)
ix_document_chunks_embedding HNSW, vector_cosine_ops, m=16
HNSW = a graph linking each vector to its near neighbours. The search starts at an
entry point and keeps stepping towards the question: it visits hundreds of vectors,
not 50,000. APPROXIMATE: it can miss a true neighbour (recall measured below).
Small organisations: the planner skips the index and compares every row (exact).
200 {"mode": "semantic", "results": [ … ]}
rank = 1 − cosine distance = cosine similarity (same score as v8)
Worker (processing.py): unchanged flow — the chunk's vector is now written to the
vector column; each insert also updates the HNSW graph.
Migration e5f1a8c3d9b2: bytea → vector(384) (exact copy), then builds the index.
WHERE THE WORK HAPPENS (50,000 chunks)
v8: PostgreSQL → 77 MB → Python → NumPy
read every vector 13,008 ms · score + sort 36 ms
cost grows with the organisation, not with limit
exact — the baseline the index is judged against
v9: PostgreSQL computes the distance, walks the index
only 5 rows cross the network
exact in SQL (no index): 1.8–2.2 s — still reads every row
HNSW index: 72–95 ms
in-process P50, same laptop, same session
THE FILTERING TRAP (found by a test)
Default: take 40 candidates, THEN apply WHERE org = …
Org 2 has 300 chunks near the question, org 1 has 3 far away.
All 40 candidates belong to org 2 → org 1 gets 0 results,
although it owns 3 chunks.
tenant isolation still holds — it is a missing-results bug, not a leak
Fix: hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order
the scan keeps walking until 5 rows pass the filter,
still sorted by distance → org 1 gets its 3 chunks
test_a_small_organisation_still_gets_its_results_from_the_index
fails with 0 == 3 when the line is removed
MEASUREMENTS (local Windows laptop, PostgreSQL in Docker, low free memory; same session unless noted)
Semantic search, 50,000 chunks, via API
v8: 10,498 ms P50 (v8 session)
v9: 147 ms P50 / 319 ms P95 (30 requests)
keyword, same run: 149 ms P50
includes embedding the question (~141 ms in v8)
synthetic chunks with random vectors, limit=5
Recall@5: index vs exact
ef_search 40 100 200
real: embedded paragraphs, 100 held-out questions
random 384-d points have no near neighbours: worst case
The price of the index (50,000 chunks)
index 98 MB, table 245 MB
build over existing rows: 137 s
insert 12,000 chunks with the index: 143 s
maintenance_work_mem 64 MB ran out at 28,364 rows
migration of the 50k database, total: 4 min
NEXT LIMITATION
• Retrieval is fast now, but it never says "nothing relevant": it always returns 5 chunks, even for questions the knowledge base cannot answer
(v8 test: score < 0.3). Generated answers (v10-rag) need a relevance threshold, chosen by measurement, before retrieved text becomes "facts".
• Embedding throughput is still 1–10 chunks/s on this CPU: a 300-page PDF takes ~7.5 min to become searchable (v8).
• Recall depends on the data: it must be re-measured on each organisation's real chunks, not assumed from the benchmark above.
Proposed next: v10-rag — relevance threshold first, then a local model that answers only from retrieved chunks, with citations.
